section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic despatches, monthly political reports, and Department of State memoranda from the American Embassy in Tokyo covering August through October 1940. It includes the concluding pages of the August telegram schedule, the complete September 1940 monthly report (Report No. 168) with related departmental summaries and transmission letters, and the initial segment of the October 1940 report (Report No. 169). The materials document critical developments in Japanese foreign and internal affairs, notably the conclusion of the Tripartite Pact with Germany and Italy, Japanese military expansion into French Indochina, disputes over Shanghai defense sectors, repeated bombings of American mission property in China, and the initiation of evacuation advice for American citizens in the Far East.

subfiles.about: Index register of telegrams dispatched by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State between August 9 and August 31, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Contains entries 678 through 771 of telegrams transmitted by the American Embassy in Tokyo to Washington during the latter half of August 1940. Subject matters include the Shanghai Marine incident of July 7, the withdrawal of British troops from China, negotiations and military demands concerning French Indochina, General Koiso's statements and proposed mission to the Netherlands East Indies, Shanghai defense sectors, anti-British demonstrations, the arrival of Ambassador Steinhardt, and Prince Konoye's statements on the new national structure.
subfiles.title: List of Telegrams Sent to the Department of State, August 1940 (Nos. 678–771)

subfiles.about: Transmittal despatch forwarding the American Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for September 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits Report 168 on September 1940 Japan conditions, distributed to Peiping, Chungking, Moscow, Bangkok, and regional posts.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5147 Transmitting Monthly Report of Conditions in Japan for September 1940
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: State Department division memorandum summarizing key economic and domestic political findings of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for September 1940.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Coville's summary of Report 168 notes restrained Tripartite Pact press commentary, a 6% stock decline, falling living costs, and Japanese Christian groups merging toward financial independence.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Report on Conditions in Japan for September 1940

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of Despatch No. 5147 transmitting Report No. 168 for September 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Despatch 5147 copy bears routing stamps from European, Commercial, and Economic Affairs divisions confirming submission of Report 168.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5147 Transmitting Monthly Report of Conditions in Japan for September 1940 (Duplicate Copy)
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Comprehensive monthly report by the American Embassy in Tokyo detailing Japan's international relations, domestic politics, economic situation, and diplomatic correspondence during September 1940.
subfiles.summary: Report No. 168 provides a comprehensive account of events in Japan during September 1940, including diplomatic disputes with the United States over Shanghai defense sectors, the July 7 Marine incident, American protests over Japanese troops entering French Indochina, and repeated bombings of American missionary properties across China. It details the secret mission of Heinrich Stahmer culminating in the conclusion of the Tripartite Pact with Germany and Italy, tensions with Great Britain over the Burma Road agreement and the arrest of Japanese subjects in Singapore, the bombing of the Canadian Pacific steamship Empress of Asia, trade negotiations in Batavia headed by Ichizo Kobayashi, and Norwegian diplomatic representation. The report also describes internal Cabinet developments such as the appointment of Admiral Oikawa as Navy Minister and General Tatekawa as Ambassador to Moscow, a severe stock market downturn, and complete monthly registers of telegrams (Nos. 772–923) and despatches (Nos. 4942–5025) sent to Washington (with page 85 misplaced from the despatch list).
subfiles.title: Report No. 168: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of September 1940

subfiles.about: State Department division memorandum summarizing the principal political and economic observations of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for October 1940.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Coville's October 1940 summary notes 600-1,000 Americans planning withdrawal, Japanese Burma Road claims, 'new structure' communism accusations, record note issuance, and an 8% rice-crop drop.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Report on Conditions in Japan for October 1940

subfiles.about: Transmittal despatch forwarding the American Embassy's monthly report on conditions in Japan for October 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Grew submits Report 169 on October 1940 Japan conditions, distributed to Peiping, Chungking, Moscow, Bangkok, regional posts, and the Asiatic Fleet commander.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5160 Transmitting Monthly Report of Conditions in Japan for October 1940
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Initial portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly report for October 1940, covering American evacuation advisories, high-level diplomatic conferences, and the Tripartite Alliance.
subfiles.summary: Report No. 169 opens with an index and summary table followed by the initial narrative on relations with the United States in October 1940. It recounts the State Department's recommendation that non-essential American citizens withdraw from the Far East, consular registrations counting 6,300 American residents in the Empire, and initial departures on commercial liners and the evacuation vessel S.S. Monterey. The text records extensive interviews between Ambassador Grew and Foreign Minister Matsuoka, including Matsuoka's formal presentation of a statement characterizing the Tripartite Pact as a defensive measure designed to establish a Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere and blaming Anglo-American assistance to Chiang Kai-shek for prolonging the conflict in China.
subfiles.title: Report No. 169: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of October 1940 (Incomplete)
